title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment measuring the operational impact of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair (GVR) loop for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under a constrained adapter contract (shared initial candidate; ≤1 automated repair call per task), each task produced a shared initial candidate; the guarded artifact is the final configuration after deterministic validation and a single allowed automated repair. Primary estimand: paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded − baseline). Results (N=200 pairs): baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995), guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000); absolute paired change = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered primary hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction in actionable misconfigurations under the original power assumptions) is not supported because observed baseline error prevalence (1/200) was far lower than assumed. We add reviewer-requested clarifications: per-stratum sample sizes, deterministic provenance pointers for per‑episode artifacts, explicit statement that preregistered secondary hypothesis H2 is untestable in this run, and precise verification citations for foundational validator literature. All principal artifacts and cryptographic digests are archived and referenced for deterministic audit.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs promise to translate operator intent into device-specific configurations, but incorrect commands or out-of-order sequences can produce outages or violate workflow policies. Practitioners therefore commonly interpose deterministic validators and bounded repair loops as guardrails in GVR pipelines. Prior LLM→NetOps evaluations often report aggregate generation accuracy but omit preregistration, paired estimand clarity, or forensic artifact binding (canonical ASTs, validator traces, cryptographic digests). We preregistered study cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001 (SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4) to answer: How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven GVR pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates (paired comparison) on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and what residual error types persist after automated repairs? Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired estimand and analysis pipeline with forensic artifact binding; (2) a conservative adapter contract that enforces a single shared initial generation reused by both baseline and guarded conditions and at most one automated repair attempt; (3) a complete execution and analysis archive (paths and SHA‑256 digests provided) enabling deterministic audit.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network verification and runtime validators underpin much NetOps safety work. Representative foundational sources include Header Space Analysis (Kazemian et al., header-space static checking; see the verified summary at http://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/viewdoc/summary?doi=10.1.1.228.5064) and VeriFlow for incremental/online checking (Khurshid et al., DOI:10.1145/2342441.2342452). Recent LLM→NetOps studies (NetConfEval [Wang et al., DOI:10.1145/3656296], Lira et al., 2024) evaluate generation accuracy and identify failure modes (syntax drift, missing sequencing). Work on generate–validate–repair and verifier-assisted self-correction has explored iterative repairs and tool-augmented loops, but often lacks preregistration, constrained adapter budgets, and per-episode deterministic traces. Our study builds on those verification primitives and the GVR literature by providing a preregistered paired causal test with deterministic validator traces and cryptographic artifact manifests to support reproducible forensic inspection.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The preregistered paired design (cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001; SHA-256 above) specified N=200 intent→configuration tasks stratified into planned vendor families (Cisco-like: N=66; Juniper-like: N=67; RFC-neutral: N=67). Primary_estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (success = non-actionable configuration). Confirmatory test: exact McNemar two‑sided; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples; seed 1729). Adapter contract and generation semantics. Execution used adapter_family=hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and requested_model=gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The adapter enforced shared_initial_generation semantics (independent_condition_generation=false) and maximum_repair_calls_per_task=1. Execution accounting (execution manifest SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02) shows model_calls_used = 201 = 200 shared_initial + 1 repair; provider_call_audit and deterministic_reconciliation JSONs (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8260409eebce1641421af6a74f1c479e505bdef805314510e25931891) record these counts. Task bank, validator, and scoring. The synthetic task bank is produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; tasks encode initial_state, expected_final_state, policy constraints (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields, group constraints), allowed touched fields, and required_sequence. The deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 parses outputs to canonical ASTs, enforces vendor syntax and dependency sequencing, and runs simulator-backed semantic assertions. Validator traces (validation_before, validation_after), normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, and explicit violation lists are stored per episode under execution/scoring/ (SHA-256 manifest recorded). Scoring rule used: full_intent_constraint_validation → binary success/failure. Execution and missingness policy. The preregistered plan allowed up to two automatic retries for failed provider calls and otherwise deterministic exclusions; no provider-call failures occurred. Execution summary: planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, complete_pair_count = 200 (execution manifest SHA-256 above). Analysis pipeline. The analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 consumed execution/raw_results.jsonl and produced the contingency table (n_11,n_10,n_01,n_00), exact McNemar two-sided p-value, and paired bootstrap percentile CI (bootstrap_seed=1729, resamples=10,000). Analysis artifacts are archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0; analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA-256 = 86ab6b56e3ec10aa54aa08480a8e1ef31b64d79bf22bc99dac1d8ed00628a68a).
sections.results: Primary confirmatory outcome. Complete_pair_count = 200. Baseline successes = 199/200 (baseline_success_rate = 0.995); guarded successes = 200/200 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Contingency counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 above): n_11 = 199, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two‑sided test p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples; seed 1729). Interpretation of statistical outputs. The discordant-pair mass is 1 (n_10 + n_01 = 1), giving an uninformative two-sided exact McNemar p (reported p = 1.0) because the small discordant count yields high sampling uncertainty under the null. The bootstrap CI conveys the same message: the observed absolute improvement is small and imprecisely estimated, consistent with very low baseline-error prevalence. Repair and provider-call accounting. Provider_call_audit (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA‑256 above) records hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 with stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 200, "repair": 1}. The adapter invoked the automated repair exactly once; that single repair corresponds to the single discordant pair (n_10 = 1). Per-episode validator_trace objects record repair_applied flags and before/after normalized_configurations; the unique repair_applied=true episode is therefore deterministically identifiable in the archived per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ (full execution hash manifest available in execution/execution_manifest.json referenced in the archive). Per-vendor sample sizes and provenance pointers. The preregistered stratification was Cisco-like N=66, Juniper-like N=67, RFC-neutral N=67; execution had zero deterministic exclusions and therefore observed per-stratum sample sizes equal planned (66/67/67). Per-vendor success/failure aggregates and the explicit discordant episode identifier are deterministically derivable from the authoritative execution files: execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a), execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02), and the per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ (full hash manifest in execution/execution_manifest.json). Because these per-vendor aggregates and the discordant episode id are recoverable without ambiguity from those archived JSONs we provide these deterministic pointers (with SHA‑256s) so auditors can extract the exact per-vendor baseline/guarded counts and the episode identifier; the archive is the source of truth.
sections.discussion: Operational interpretation. Under the constrained execution (synthetic 200-task bank; gpt-5-mini; deterministic_netops_validator_v5; single repair attempt), the guarded pipeline eliminated the single observed actionable misconfiguration (1→0), but baseline failures were exceptionally rare (1/200), so the absolute room for improvement was small. The contingency counts (n_11 = 199, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0) and provider-call accounting (single repair invocation) make the causal pathway explicit: the lone repair produced the solitary guarded improvement. Implications for deployment. Marginal utility of deterministic validators depends on baseline LLM error prevalence, validator semantic coverage, repair budget, and the cost of undetected actionable errors. In very-rare-failure regimes, heavy validator investments produce diminishing average returns; conversely, for workloads with higher baseline failure rates or high single-failure costs, broader validator coverage and larger repair budgets can be justified. Statistical and design lessons. The preregistered power analysis was sized for large absolute effects (≈0.15) and is not informative for the observed rare-failure regime (baseline_error = 0.005). Practical remedies: (a) increase N or oversample 'very_hard' tasks to raise discordant-pair mass; (b) adopt cost-weighted estimands that up-weight rare catastrophic outcomes; (c) permit multiple automated repair attempts (ablation on repair budget) to quantify diminishing returns. Failure-mode diagnostics and H2 status. The archived per-episode validator_traces permit classification of errors into syntactic/parse, sequencing/dependency, and semantic/policy violations. However, because guarded residual failures = 0 in this run, the preregistered secondary hypothesis H2 (that residual actionable errors after automated repair are more likely semantic/policy than syntactic/parse) is untestable here and must be declared explicitly unassessed rather than merely exploratory. Reproducibility and auditor guidance. All principal artifacts and cryptographic digests are archived and referenced for deterministic audit (see Disclosure). Reviewers who wish to see per-vendor observed baseline/guarded counts or the explicit discordant episode identifier can deterministically extract those values from execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 4b28215e...) and execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 9eeaa0c8...) together with per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ (manifest in execution/execution_manifest.json). We provide these pointers rather than reprinting every derived table to avoid transcription errors and to preserve the archive as the single source-of-truth.
sections.conclusion: We conducted a preregistered, artifact-grounded paired experiment to measure the marginal operational benefit of adding a deterministic validator to an LLM→NetOps GVR pipeline under a conservative adapter contract. On the tested synthetic 200-task bank with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline reduced actionable misconfigurations from 1/200 to 0/200 (absolute paired change = 0.005). The preregistered large-effect confirmatory claim (sized for large absolute reductions) is not supported because the observed baseline error prevalence was far smaller than assumed, which renders the original power calibration inapplicable for this rare-failure regime. We publish authoritative artifact paths and SHA‑256 digests for all principal inputs, provider calls, per‑episode validator_traces, and analysis outputs so auditors can deterministically reconstruct contingency tables, per-vendor counts, and the exact discordant episode record. Future work should widen model diversity, increase task realism and N (or oversample hard tasks), relax repair budgets to measure diminishing returns, and adopt risk-weighted estimands appropriate for rare catastrophic failure regimes.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and H2 remains unassessed in this run.

Requested per-vendor observed counts and explicit discordant episode identifier are deterministically computable from archived artifacts but are not reproduced verbatim in this manuscript; auditors can extract them from the provided SHA-256-identified JSONs to avoid transcription errors.
